title: Account vending and guardrails (SCPs and policies)
hook: Account vending automatically creates new AWS accounts with baseline security and networking applied. Guardrails — especially Service Control Policies (SCPs) — set maximum permissions for entire organizational units.

blocks.text: Account Factory (Control Tower) or custom Step Functions workflow creates accounts, assigns to OU, and triggers StackSets for logging, Config, IAM baseline. SCPs are organization policies attached to OUs/accounts that filter IAM permissions — they do not grant access, only deny. Preventive guardrails block actions; detective guardrails (Config) detect drift.
Interviewers ask "how do you stop a developer from opening S3 to the world org-wide?" SCP deny on public buckets. Account vending ensures every account starts compliant, not retrofitted.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: SCPs are permission guardrails on OUs; vending automates compliant account creation.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Define SCP policies
items.body: Deny risky actions: unapproved regions, disable CloudTrail, public S3 ACLs.

items.title: Attach to OUs
items.body: Sandbox gets stricter limits than Production OU.

items.title: Vend account
items.body: Account Factory creates account, applies baseline stacks.

items.title: Validate enrollment
items.body: Control Tower dashboard shows control status per account.

snippet.label: SCP deny unapproved regions
snippet.explanation: Data residency guardrail — common enterprise SCP.

snippet.label: SCP protect CloudTrail
snippet.explanation: Preventive guardrail — audit trail cannot be disabled.

snippet.label: Create SCP and attach
snippet.code:
aws organizations create-policy \
  --name DenyPublicS3 --type SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY \
  --content file://deny-public-s3.json
aws organizations attach-policy \
  --policy-id p-abc --target-id ou-xyz
snippet.explanation: Attach SCP to OU — applies to all accounts underneath.

snippet.label: Provision Account Factory account
snippet.code:
aws servicecatalog provision-product \
  --product-id prod-abc \
  --provisioning-artifact-id pa-xyz \
  --provisioned-product-name team-payments-dev
snippet.explanation: Self-service account vending with baseline stacks.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: SCP that blocks Control Tower management actions — breaks landing zone. SCP thinking it grants permissions. No break-glass exception process.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: SCP simulator tests before attach; 100% account enrollment in Control Tower; Config compliance % per OU; time-to-vend new account < 1 hour.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Confusing SCP with IAM policy — rejected. Strong answer: SCP filters max permissions; IAM grants within that boundary.

interviewTakeaways: SCPs set permission ceiling for OUs — deny only, never grant.
Account vending applies baselines at creation — not retrofit.
Preventive (SCP) + detective (Config) guardrails complement each other.
60s: SCP on OU denies risky APIs org-wide. Account Factory vends compliant accounts. Test SCPs in simulator. Break-glass OU for emergencies.
Follow-up: what happens when SCP and IAM both allow an action?
commonPitfalls: SCP grants permissions — wrong; SCP only denies/filters.
Strong answer: IAM grants within SCP ceiling; explicit deny in SCP wins.
SCP blocks Control Tower — landing zone breaks.
No break-glass process for SCP-blocked emergencies.

jsTsCorrelations.note: SCP JSON mirrors OPA/authorization middleware — deny rules at org boundary.
SCP ceiling like TypeScript strict mode — limits what code can do at compile boundary.
